Maximization of the Integrand for Generalized Linear Gaussian Process Models

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
maxim_integrand.Rd

Finds the conditional mode of the latent effects in a binomial or Poisson generalized linear Gaussian process model (GLGPM), that is, the maximiser of the joint log-density of the responses and the latent spatial and unstructured random effects, viewed as a function of the latent effects.

Usage

maxim_integrand(
  y,
  denominator,
  mu,
  Sigma,
  ID_coords,
  ID_re = NULL,
  family,
  sigma2_re = NULL,
  hessian = FALSE,
  gradient = FALSE,
  invlink = NULL
)

Arguments

y

Response variable vector: numbers of positives for family = "binomial", or counts for family = "poisson".

denominator

Numeric vector with one positive value per response: the number of trials for family = "binomial", or the exposure (the expected count is denominator times the inverse link of the linear predictor) for family = "poisson". This is the same quantity as the denominator argument of glgpm().

mu

Vector of the fixed part of the linear predictor, one value per response.

Sigma

Covariance matrix of the spatial process.

ID_coords

Indices mapping response to locations.

ID_re

Indices mapping response to unstructured random effects.

family

The distribution of the response, "binomial" or "poisson", a binomial or Poisson family object with one of the links that glgpm() accepts, such as binomial("probit"), or negative_binomial() with its size, such as negative_binomial(theta = 2), with denominator the exposure.

sigma2_re

Variance of the unstructured random effects.

hessian

Logical; if TRUE, compute the Hessian matrix.

gradient

Logical; if TRUE, compute the gradient vector.

invlink

A function that maps the linear predictor to the mean of the response given the random effects, for a link that family does not name, as in glgpm().

Value

A list with the mode (mode), the name of the inverse link used (invlink_used) and either the Hessian of the integrand at the mode (hessian, if hessian = TRUE) or the inverse of its negative (Sigma.tilde, otherwise). If gradient = TRUE, the gradient at the mode is also returned (gradient).

Details

The mode is found by Newton-type optimisation (stats::nlminb()) using the analytic gradient and Hessian of the integrand. The integrand includes terms for the spatial process (Sigma), the unstructured random effects (sigma2_re), and the log-likelihood of the responses for the specified family. With the canonical links, the terms of a response whose probability rounds to 0 or 1, or whose mean underflows to 0, are computed in their exact canonical form, so that the optimisation is not stopped there.

Examples

coords <- cbind(c(0, 1, 2), c(0, 0, 1))
Sigma <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(coords)))
mode <- maxim_integrand(
  y = c(3, 5, 1), denominator = c(10, 10, 10), mu = rep(-0.5, 3),
  Sigma = Sigma, ID_coords = 1:3, family = "binomial"
)
mode$mode
#> [1] -0.1997816  0.2532412 -0.8857314
